claim: DCAR-1 is required for the epidermal response to fungal infection and wounding, and HPLA is its endogenous ligand
key_finding: Genome-wide RNAi screen identified DCAR-1; it acts in the epidermis to regulate antimicrobial peptide expression via p38 MAPK; targeted metabolomics identified 4-hydroxyphenyllactic acid as the endogenous ligand
context: C. elegans, epidermis, in vivo RNAi and nlp-29 reporter; ligand identified by metabolomics and applied exogenously
confidence: High for the genetic requirement, moderate for direct receptor-ligand engagement; no binding assay, no purified receptor, no structure

evidence_type: structural (contacts recomputed here from deposited coordinates)
claim: HCAR-family receptors anchor the ligand carboxylate with Arg3.36 and hydrogen bond it with Tyr7.43
key_finding: Measured directly: 8IJA R111 2.72 A, Y284 2.61 A; 9JKT R111 2.83 A, Y284 2.90 A; 8IHJ R111 2.62 A. HCAR3 pocket volume 75 A3 with the ligand removed, 100% ligand-atom recovery by the cavity detector
confidence: High. These are the correct comparators: 9JKT ligand HF2 (D-phenyllactate) is the des-hydroxy analogue of HPLA

citation: This analysis (AlphaFold AF-G5EDI0-v6 + GPCRdb generic numbering)
claim: DCAR-1 carries an HCAR-like carboxylate-binding Arg3.36 and Tyr7.43
key_finding: DCAR-1 has Phe at 3.36 (F120) and Phe at 7.43 (F302). No basic residue sits at any anchor position used by acid receptors (3.29, 3.33, 3.36, 5.39, 6.58, 7.35, 7.39). TM3 register confirmed twice: GPCRdb offset resi-BWindex = 84 at six TM3 anchors, and F116 superposes on HCAR3 F107 at 1.30 A
context: Predicted model, pLDDT 87-94 in the pocket region
confidence: High for the residue identities, moderate for the exact BW register of TM7 (a one-residue shift would change which TM7 face lines the pocket)

claim: A carboxylate-binding basic residue at 3.36 is conserved in nematode DCAR-1 orthologues
key_finding: 3.36 is Phe in 17/18 and never basic; 7.43 is F/A/T and never Tyr. 58-94% identity, Caenorhabditis spp., Diploscapter pachys, Heligmosomoides polygyrus, Angiostrongylus costaricensis
context: Sequence only; UniRef50 cluster membership used because the EBI BLAST REST endpoint refused new jobs
confidence: High for the C. elegans group, lower outside it because the cluster is dominated by Caenorhabditis

citation: This analysis (BW superposition of AF-G5EDI0 on 9JKT, ligand transfer)
claim: DCAR-1 has no basic residue facing the orthosteric space at all
key_finding: R300 (7.41) is invariant in 18/18 homologues and lies 0.85 A from the transferred ligand centroid, salt-bridged to E113 (3.29, Glu in 17/18) at 2.56 A. The ligand position itself is 1.33 A from protein atoms, that is, occluded in the apo model
confidence: Moderate. The pair is a model-derived feature; apo models routinely close pockets, so this is a hypothesis for mutagenesis, not a demonstrated ligand contact

claim: Fold-level similarity can assign DCAR-1 to a ligand class
key_finding: Identity to all references 18-26% (rhodopsin 25.9%); TM-bundle RMSD 1.29-1.81 A for acid and peptide receptors alike; apo AlphaFold cavity volumes do not track ligand size (HCAR2 460, HCAR3 337, GHSR 648, NTSR1 448 A3)
context: Ten reference structures, four apo control models
confidence: High. These measures are uninformative here and must not be used to justify a GO call

claim: DCAR-1 is a small-molecule acid receptor
key_finding: PTHR24243 human members are peptide receptors (NTSR1, NTSR2, NMUR1, NMUR2, CCKBR, MLNR, GHSR); C. elegans members include dcar-1 with nmur-1/2/3, npr-21, npr-35, sphr-1. Best pairwise hit for DCAR-1 is C. elegans NMUR-1 at 30.8%
context: Family assignment by HMM, the basis of the existing IBA neuropeptide receptor activity annotation
confidence: Moderate. Family membership does not fix ligand class, and it conflicts with the HPLA genetics

claim: DCAR-1 is a canonical class A GPCR whose pocket can be read off a human template
key_finding: Keeps D2.50 (D84), W4.50 (W161), P6.50 (P268), D7.49-P7.50 (D310-P311); lacks D(E)RY (L133-K134-L135), CWxP Trp (6.48 = M266, Asn in 12/18 homologues) and NPxxY Tyr (7.53 = A314). Model predicts C9-C283 and C189-C194, not C3.25-C45.50
confidence: High for the motif calls. Divergence this deep limits how far any human template transfers
